rows.evidence: Q1: Methods <U+2013> three-year (2013<U+2013>2016) field experiment in a Beijing greenhouse, four treatments (CK, FP, FPD, RFPD) x three replicates, N2O flux, yield, NUE and IWUE measured. Q2: Table 3 and Results 'Vegetable yields, NUE and IWUE' <U+2013> RFPD (drip + 40% less urea-N) gave mean annual cucumber 100 vs 96 t/ha and celery 97 vs 94 t/ha compared with FP; authors state reducing synthetic N by 40% with drip had no negative impact on yields; Table 4 NUE 131 vs 105 kg/kg (+25%). Q4: Fig. 1c and 1e <U+2013> soil WFPS (15 cm) and topsoil NO3- measured per treatment through the whole period; discussion links higher yield/NUE under RFPD to drip meeting plant N and water needs with measured soil moisture and nitrate differences. rows.notes: Passage says yield was 'significantly improved'; the study shows celery yield significantly higher under RFPD than FP but cucumber RFPD (100ab) not significantly different from FP (96b), i.e. yield maintained rather than clearly improved. Q4 counted on measured soil water and nitrate as intermediates; mechanism for yield is partly inferred in discussion.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods <U+2013> three-year greenhouse field experiment with four irrigation/fertilisation treatments and three replicates. Q2: Table 4 and Results <U+2013> IWUE of drip treatments significantly higher than flood over the whole period; RFPD increased mean annual IWUE by 40% (45 vs 32 kg/m3) and FPD by 37% relative to FP; Table 1 shows drip applied less water per season for the same number of events. Q4: Fig. 1c and auxiliary measurements <U+2013> irrigation volumes recorded by water meter and soil WFPS at 15 cm measured in each treatment (mean 58<U+2013>59% under drip vs 61% under flood), the soil-water intermediate between irrigation method and water productivity. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' <U+2013> single site and cropping pattern in NCP, larger-scale application needs verification with multi-year monitoring; discussion notes low temporal resolution of moisture monitoring may have missed short-term WFPS changes.
rows.notes: IWUE is a calculated ratio of yield to metered irrigation water (one method). Table 4 reports IWUE with significance letters only, no standard errors, so Q9 is no. No condition required for the IWUE gain is stated from own findings.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods <U+2013> three-year greenhouse field experiment, four treatments x three replicates. Q2: Table 4 and Results <U+2013> RFPD (drip + 40% less urea-N) increased mean annual IWUE by 40% and NUE by 25% vs FP; Table 2 <U+2013> mean annual N2O under RFPD reduced by 45% vs FP; Table 3 <U+2013> celery yield under RFPD 97 vs 94 t/ha (maintained/increased). Q4: Fig. 1c <U+2013> soil WFPS at 15 cm measured through the whole period under drip vs flood, plus metered irrigation volumes (Table 1), the intermediate through which drip improves water productivity. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' <U+2013> results from one cropping pattern at one NCP site, regional/national application needs multi-year verification; discussion acknowledges moisture monitoring resolution too low to capture post-irrigation WFPS peaks.
rows.notes: Figures in the passage (45% N2O reduction, 40% IWUE, 25% NUE, celery yield maintained) match the abstract and Tables 2<U+2013>4. IWUE reported without dispersion measure (letters only), so Q9 no.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods <U+2013> three-year greenhouse field experiment, four treatments x three replicates, yields weighed at each harvest. Q2: Table 3 <U+2013> mean annual celery yield 97 t/ha under RFPD vs 94 under FP (significantly higher), cucumber 100 vs 96 (not significantly different); authors conclude 40% synthetic-N reduction with drip did not negatively affect cucumber or celery yields; Table 4 <U+2013> NUE 131 vs 105 kg/kg. Q4: Fig. 1c and 1e <U+2013> soil WFPS and topsoil NO3- measured per treatment, discussed as the basis for drip meeting crop water and N needs. Q7: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' <U+2013> authors state the recommended N rate under drip should account for planting conditions, crop requirements and initial soil N content, since the yield gap in unfertilised plots only appeared in S4 owing to high initial soil organic matter and NO3-. Q8: same section <U+2013> one cropping pattern and site, larger-scale application needs verification; need for multi-year observation stressed. Q9: Table 3 <U+2013> yields reported as means <U+00B1> standard errors.
rows.notes: Celery yield was maintained or increased under RFPD; S4 celery yield was lower under RFPD than FP (80 vs 90) while mean annual was higher, so 'stability' holds only on the multi-year mean.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single-site, single-greenhouse plot experiment (8 m x 6 m plots) in the North China Plain with one soil type; two crops (cucumber, celery) in rotation. Technology in the study is drip fertigation, matching the passages. IWUE and NUE are reported without standard errors; N2O and yield with standard errors.
